sections.label: Chemical Weapons Prohibition Act enactment
sections.summary: In 2000 Singapore enacted the CWPA to give effect to CWC obligations and established a licence system for scheduled chemicals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2000, Singapore enacted the Chemical Weapons (Prohibition) Act, or CWPA for short, to give effect to our international obligations under CWC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: Under the CWPA, Singapore established a licence system to control various activities involving chemicals listed under CWC, known as "scheduled chemicals", for a permitted purpose.

sections.label: Controls on Schedule 1 chemicals
sections.summary: The CWPA controls movement within Singapore of Schedule 1 chemicals but not Schedules 2 and 3 chemicals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: It also provides for controls on the movement within Singapore of Schedule 1 chemicals, which are the most dangerous category of chemicals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: However, the CWPA does not impose controls on the movement of Schedules 2 and 3 chemicals within Singapore.

sections.label: New sections 9A and 9B
sections.summary: Clause 6 enacts new sections 9A and 9B of the CWPA to ensure proper controls for movement of all scheduled chemicals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: First, to ensure proper controls for the movement of all scheduled chemicals within Singapore, clause 6 enacts new sections 9A and 9B of the CWPA.

sections.label: Powers of national inspectors
sections.summary: New powers let national inspectors stop and board vehicles, seize items, and arrest individuals under certain circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: The new powers will allow national inspectors to: (a) stop and board the vehicle; (b) seize any item from the vehicle which the inspector reasonably believes to be the subject matter of, or connected with the commission of, an offence under section 9A; and (c) arrest an individual under certain circumstances.

sections.label: Regulations prescribing imprisonment and consultation
sections.summary: Regulations may prescribe imprisonment up to two years, and 101 companies consulted in September 2018 were generally amenable to amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: In addition, regulations may now prescribe imprisonment for up to two years instead of just fines, on the conviction of any offence prescribed in the regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: In September 2018, Singapore Customs conducted an industry consultation and reached out to 101 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
sentences.text: Based on the feedback received, the companies were generally amenable to the proposed amendments.

sections.label: Risk of chemical weapons attack
sections.summary: Although the risk of a terrorist attack in Singapore involving chemical weapons is low, the possibility cannot be ruled out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Although the risk of a terrorist attack in Singapore involving chemical weapons is low, we cannot rule out the possibility that it might happen.

sections.label: CWC licence applicant screening
sections.summary: CWC licence applicants and drivers are screened for red flags such as United Nations sanctions violations before licence or permit issuance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The main and alternate CWC licence applicants are screened for any red flags, such as violations of United Nations sanctions, before a licence is granted to them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Drivers will also be screened before they are issued with a Hazmat Transport Driver Permit (HTDP).

sections.label: Transport of scheduled chemicals
sections.summary: The current amendments cover the transport of prescribed scheduled chemicals in a vehicle by public road.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The current amendments cover the transport of prescribed scheduled chemicals in a vehicle by public road.
